title: Additional security under clause 4.20 — writ dismissed following Dev Prayag
coram: Shekhar B. Saraf, J.; Prashant Kumar, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed; additional-security demand under clause 4.20 not bad.
headnote: A consumer challenged Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.'s 12.05.2014 demand for additional security, attributed to clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. After a 2014 interim restraint, a Division Bench dismissed the writ in 2025, following M/s Dev Prayag Paper Mill (Pvt.) v. State of U.P. (Writ-C No. 30898 of 2016, 21.03.2017), which held that a distribution licensee's demand of additional security is not bad.
facts: M/s Jai Hanuman Rice Mill (computer-corrected to M/s Jai Hanuman Chawal Udyog) received from Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. a 12.05.2014 demand for additional security, said to be under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005. It sought quashing of that notice, relying on an interim order in Supreme Ceramics (W.P. No. 51844 of 2009). On 27.05.2014 the Court connected the matter with W.P. (C) No. 51884 of 2009 and restrained the additional-security demand until further orders; the petitioner's name was later corrected.

holding_units.holding: A writ seeking to quash a distribution licensee's demand of additional security under clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 stands dismissed on the reasoning in Dev Prayag Paper Mill: such a demand is not bad.
